The canon by co-citation

The people History PhDs cite, with the theses taken out: two people are linked when theses cite them both, and the link's weight is that number of theses. 4,894 people cited by at least 40 of 13,996 strict History PhDs (all countries); the filter hides people cited by fewer theses and redraws the map for those left.

How to read this

  • Co-citation count is the raw number of theses whose bibliographies cite both people (any of their works). It grows with size, so the most cited theorists (Foucault, Anderson, Hobsbawm, Bourdieu) become hubs and the map shows the canon's core and its reach. Association strength divides by what the two citation counts would give by chance (as in VOSviewer), so people sit with those who share their readers, which brings out fields rather than fame.
  • Each person keeps their 5 strongest links among the people shown, pairs cited together by at least 5 theses. Positions come from a spring layout of those links, computed for each filter step; the axes mean nothing. People with no link to the main map at a step are not drawn.
  • Colour: a person leans to a region when its share of History PhDs citing them is at least 1.5 times the next region's (Canada 2,249, United States 3,088, Britain 2,656, Brazil 2,618, Rest of Europe 2,494, elsewhere 891 theses). Hollow circles have no reviewed Wikidata QID; most are real historians, but a few common names may merge namesakes.
  • People are the authors of cited works as the graph resolves them (namesakes split through the cited titles). Stray tokens, government bodies and initial-only names without a QID are left out. A citation is not engagement.

Built 2026-11-05 (scripts/historian_cocitation_network.py); every pair co-cited by at least 5 theses is in summary/network/historian-cocitation-pairs.csv. See also the map of the most cited works.
